fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sep-2027 ~$4.40 x 19x = $84), FCF yield (FY28 FCF ~$2.4B at 4.8% yield less ~$4B net debt = $80) and EV/EBITDA (FY28 EBITDA ~$3.0B x 16x less net debt = $77); weighted to ~$82.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS as of Sep-2027 ~$4.40 (FY27 run-rate: Q1 $0.76, Q2 guide $0.91-0.95, H2 ~$1.00-1.05 -> FY27 ~$3.7; FY28 ~$4.3-4.5 assuming revenue ~$6.8B, GM ~65%, flat share count ~575M) x 19x (mid-cycle forward multiple for MCHP 15-22x, discounted for peak-cycle margins above 65% LT model)

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF ~$2.4B (Q1 FY27 FCF $498M on $1.485B sales, capex ~$100M/yr); required FCF yield on EV 4.8% -> EV ~$50B; less net debt ~$4.0B by Sep-2027 (from $5.2B, all excess FCF to debt paydown) -> equity ~$46B / 575M shares

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY28 EBITDA ~$3.0B (sales ~$6.8B x ~44% EBITDA margin) x 16x = $48B EV; less ~$4.0B net debt -> $44B / 575M shares

bear.story: Cycle peaks in H1 2027: double-ordering unwinds as lead times normalize, direct-OEM inventory correction and price increases reverse, GM falls back to ~60%, FY28 EPS ~$3.0; stock de-rates to ~16x on trough fears (similar to 2024-25 drawdown to high-$40s).

base.story: Upcycle continues at a slower pace; revenue ~$6.6-7.0B run-rate, GM ~65%, NTM EPS ~$4.4, data center ~$1B+ growing; net leverage falls below 2x; stock trades ~19x forward plus dividend.

bull.story: Extended AI/data-center and industrial/defense-driven cycle, supply constraints ease letting revenue reach $1.9-2B/quarter, EPS run-rate $5.5+, buybacks/dividend growth resume, semis re-rate; ~22x on $5.5.

thesis_break_reason: A move to ~$52 (-34%, ~20% below where the stock bottomed after the summer 2026 chip selloff) would imply the market is pricing EPS back near $3 or a sub-15x multiple, i.e. that the recovery has rolled over (bookings below 1, guidance cuts, GM back to ~60%) or leverage/financing stress re-emerged, rather than ordinary semiconductor beta.

catalysts.event: Q2 FY27 earnings (guide $1.589-1.618B sales, 66-67% GM, $0.91-0.95 EPS) and December-quarter guidance
Q3 FY27 earnings; read on seasonality and whether price increases stick
Q4 FY27 earnings and FY28 outlook; possible resumption of capital returns once net leverage < 2x
Q1 FY28 earnings; cycle-duration test (mgmt flagged typical 8-quarter upcycle)
Semiconductor sector sentiment / AI capex (SOX fell ~29% from June 2026 peak), TI/NXP/ADI results as read-throughs
Hailo integration (closed 2026-09-21), J Capital short thesis on data-center revenue, COO departure

key_uncertainties: Duration of the analog/MCU upcycle: book-to-bill well above 1 and stretched lead times can signal double-ordering that unwinds sharply
Sustainability of 66-67% gross margin, which management says includes one-time benefits (licensing, price increases, low write-offs)
Data-center growth credibility (~$1B CY2026 per mgmt vs short-seller skepticism)
Semiconductor sector multiple after the 2026 AI-chip boom and correction; high beta (50% realized vol)
Foundry/OSAT supply constraints capping revenue and raising costs
Estimates for FY28 not verified from a consensus source; my EPS path is extrapolated from guidance
reasoning: MCHP is in a sharp cyclical recovery: June-quarter sales $1.485B (+38% y/y, +13% q/q), non-GAAP EPS $0.76, FCF $498M, and September-quarter guidance of ~$1.60B, 66-67% GM and $0.91-0.95 EPS, with the strongest bookings in four years, distribution inventory down to 25 days, and net debt/EBITDA falling toward 2.5x. Yet the stock is $78.69, ~26% below the May high of $105.91, mainly because of the broad semiconductor selloff from the June peak (SOX -29%), plus a J Capital short report, PT cuts on inventory/margin worries (Wells $88, TD Cowen $90, UBS $120), COO departure and skepticism about the Hailo purchase. At $78.69 the stock is ~21x FY27 EPS (~$3.7) and ~18x my NTM EPS by Sep-2027 (~$4.4); the market is clearly discounting a cycle peak. My fair value (~$82, blend of P/E, FCF yield and EV/EBITDA) is only modestly above spot because I apply peak-cycle discipline: management itself says margins won't go higher and upcycles typically last ~8 quarters, which would put the peak around mid-2027 — right at the horizon, when the market will be looking at FY29 earnings. Analyst average PT ~$100-108 (range $80-135) is noted as evidence of sell-side optimism but I don't anchor on it. Scenarios: bear $50 (25%), base $85 (50%), bull $125 (25%), probability-weighted ~$86. For the ladder I used a mixture of lognormals (80% weight median $84, sigma 0.40; 20% weight median $70, sigma 0.60) to reflect 50% realized vol, a semiconductor fat left tail and slight positive drift (dividend ~2.3% not in price). This puts P(>=79) ~0.535, median ~$81, and ~27% chance of exceeding $106 (the 52-week high). Research note: Twelve Data estimates/statistics endpoints were unavailable; FY28 EPS is my own extrapolation.
